notes: Iter 1: revert TerminationsCfg.success back to mdp.cube_0_stacked_on_cube_1 (single-pair) and cube_dropped to mdp.cube_0_dropping. Per user analysis: iter_000's 0% stack rate is partially because the 3-tier success termination never fires, so the policy never gets the 'succeed and end episode' signal that the 2-cube task used. Also bumped timesteps 20M -> 30M. Cube_2 stays in scene as clutter (we may revisit later).

iters.design: 2-cube LiftCube reward (7 terms) + 3-cube env (cube_2 in scene, 3-tier success termination, 41-D obs); 20M
iters.diagnosis: Cube_0 reached + lifted ~17% of frames but never lands precisely on cube_1. Compared to iter_023 historical (same reward on 2-cube env): cube_0_stacked_bonus 37.8 -> 0. Two contributing factors: (1) 3-tier success termination never fires so episodes don't end on stage-1 success; (2) added cube_2 + larger 41-D obs make the value head slower to converge.
iters.decision: iter 1 - revert success/cube_dropped to 2-cube semantics; bump timesteps to 30M.

iters.design: 2-cube reward (7 terms) + 3-cube env + REVERTED 2-cube termination semantics (success=cube_0_stacked_on_cube_1, cube_dropped=cube_0_dropping); 30M
iters.diagnosis: BREAKTHROUGH. Reverting success termination to single-pair cube_0_stacked_on_cube_1 fixed the iter_000 failure mode. Policy converges to 99.7% stack rate; episodes end in ~40 steps (vs 250 cap). User diagnosis was exactly right: the 3-tier success termination withheld the early-end signal that PPO needs to lock in the stacking skill.
iters.decision: iter 1 verifies one-cube stacking works reliably. Next: scale to 2-cube tower (cube_1 on cube_2) by extending reward + termination.

iters.design: 3-tier success (cube_0 on cube_1 AND cube_2 on cube_0); success_bonus → cube_0_stacked_bonus_once_per_episode w=300; 30M
iters.diagnosis: Stage 1 (cube_0 on cube_1) reliably solved at 93.9% per-episode rate via the once-per-episode bonus. Stage 2 (cube_2 on cube_0) never attempted — no reward signal pulls policy toward cube_2. Episodes run to time-out (249.6/250). After the once-per-episode bonus fires, the per-frame shaping (reaching/lifting/coarse) keeps incentivizing the policy to hover cube_0 near goal rather than settle and move on.
iters.decision: iter 3 should add cube_2 shaping terms (reach/lift/place on top of cube_0).

iters.design: cube_0 success requires release (gripper not in contact with cube_0); new reaching_cube_2 + lifting_cube_2 (each w=1.0) gated on cube_0-stacked-once latch; 9 terms total; 30M
iters.diagnosis: Stage 1 (cube_0 stacked + released) at 92.7% — release-required check works. Stage 2 reaching: EE moves toward cube_2 (mean 12.51). Stage 2 lifting: ~0.3% — policy almost never grasps/lifts cube_2. Visual confirms: cube_0 ends up stacked on cube_1, EE then hovers near cube_2 but does not grasp.
iters.decision: iter 4 should encourage cube_2 LIFTING (the bottleneck). Options: boost lifting_cube_2 weight, add a transport/goal-tracking term toward cube_0 top, add a cube_2 stacking sparse bonus.

iters.design: cube_2 reach/lift gated on cube_0_currently_stacked_on_cube_1_indicator (current-frame geometric, no latch); 9 terms total; 100M timesteps
iters.diagnosis: Stage-1 improved (96.1%). Stage-2 REGRESSED — currently-stacked gate is too strict: when policy releases cube_0 and moves toward cube_2, cube_0 often shifts out of the success band, gate closes, cube_2 reward shuts off. Policy never learns to MAINTAIN the cube_0 stack while engaging cube_2. Also: entropy collapsed to -5.4 (extreme overconfidence) — PPO at 100M with ent_coef=0 lost all exploration. Visual confirms: EE briefly grasps cube_0, may stack momentarily, but then disturbs the stack while moving toward cube_2 area.
iters.decision: iter 5: cube_2 stage needs either (a) stronger lift weight, (b) tolerance for brief unstacking, (c) a transport/place reward toward cube_0_top, or (d) entropy bonus. Awaiting user direction.

iters.design: reaching_cube_2 + lifting_cube_2 weights 1.0→10.0; gate stays currently-stacked geometric; 100M timesteps
iters.diagnosis: Stage 1 mastered (98.3%). Stage-2 reaching dramatically improved with w=10: policy maintains cube_0 on cube_1 (goal_tracking 33.66→59.02 = ~0.74 per-frame value, mean cube_0-to-goal d≈4cm) AND moves EE near cube_2. BUT lifting_cube_2 still ~0.2% — policy never closes gripper on cube_2 after releasing cube_0. Entropy collapsed to -5.4. Visual: cube_0 stack visible, EE then hovers near cube_2 region without grasping.
iters.decision: iter 6 — grasping cube_2 is the new bottleneck. Options: (a) goal-tracking term for cube_2 (toward cube_0+CUBE_SIZE) gated on cube_2 lifted, (b) explicit gripper-near-cube_2 reward to bootstrap grasp, (c) much higher lifting_cube_2 weight (e.g. 50-100).

iters.design: release check switched from contact-sensor force=0 to EE-distance >= 4cm from cube_0 (applied to success_bonus + termination cube_0 leg). cube_2 weights stay 10/10. 100M timesteps
iters.diagnosis: EE-distance release criterion produces almost identical behavior to contact-based: 97.9% stage-1, strong cube_2 reaching (244.15), zero lifting (0.000). Policy stacks cube_0, moves EE 4cm+ away (now into cube_2 vicinity), but never closes gripper on cube_2. The bottleneck is gripper closure: binary lift indicator only fires AFTER cube_2 is airborne, but the close-gripper action itself has no shaping. Entropy collapsed (-5.25). Visual confirms (f007): clean cube_0-on-cube_1 stack with EE retracted, but cube_2 stays on table.
iters.decision: Stage-2 grasping is the bottleneck. Awaiting user direction.

iters.design: Added stack_broke_penalty (w=-100, once per episode when cube_0_stacked_once latch set AND cube_0 no longer geometrically on cube_1). 10 reward terms total. 100M timesteps.
iters.diagnosis: Stack stability dramatically improved: ~88.8% of episodes maintain cube_0 stack after the success bonus fires. cube_0 goal_tracking went UP (55.49→65.21, mean d cube_0-to-goal ~3cm). Stage-2 reaching went UP (244→428) — EE parks near cube_2 even more aggressively. But lifting_cube_2 STILL 0 — gripper closure on cube_2 not learned. Entropy collapsed deeper (-7.55).
iters.decision: Stage-2 grasping bottleneck unchanged. Awaiting user direction.

iters.design: Added hand_contact ContactSensorCfg (panda_hand body). Success criteria now requires geometric + EE-distance ≥4cm + no contact (fingers + hand body) vs cube_0. reaching_cube_2 weight 10→1; lifting_cube_2 stays 10. 10 reward terms; 100M.
iters.diagnosis: No-contact constraint made stage-1 stricter — success rate dropped 99.2%→92.8%. Hand body contact is hard to avoid because to geometrically stack cube_0 the gripper must be directly above the cube. Reducing reaching_cube_2 to 1.0 pulled the policy back away from cube_2 (reaching mean is normalized 3× lower per-frame). Lifting_cube_2 still 0 — no grasp. Entropy collapsed less (−3.07 vs −7.55) — the harder constraint preserved some exploration.
iters.decision: Stage-2 grasp still blocked. Awaiting direction.

best_partial_success_rate_note: iter_005 highest stage-1 rate at 98.3% (294.9/300). Stage-2 reaching dramatically improved (321.94 with w=10) but lifting still ~0.2%. Full-tower success still 0%.
